body.rationale: IPS status: ratified (this brief says so; the draft/owner_approved wording in the template does not apply). I am the market-cap-weight diagnostic and I breach the drawdown limit, so I rank only on the merits of the others. I favour portfolios that clear every hard IPS limit and lean on the covariance structure, which fits the late-cycle reasoning in the paper's section 4.3. Four candidates have no hard breaches: black_litterman, resampled_efficient_frontier, inverse_volatility and cvar_minimization. 1) black_litterman has the most drawdown headroom of the compliant return-optimised portfolios (-21.9%) and a backtest Sharpe of 0.68. Its main flaw, an AUM-based equilibrium prior that double-counts overlapping equity funds, is an input problem and can be fixed. 2) resampled_efficient_frontier is compliant and well diversified (effective N 13.1). The reviewers note that its -24.84% drawdown sits only 16bp inside the limit, so I rank it second. 3) inverse_volatility needs no return forecast, has effective N 14.8, and its backtest drawdown is -22.9%. Its reviewers found only minor wording errors, though it cannot see the correlated credit cluster of about 43% of the weight. 4) cvar_minimization is the only non-traditional method that clears the IPS, and it adds tail-aware diversity to the ensemble. It is concentrated (about 2.9 effective assets) and its volatility was tuned to land exactly on the 8% floor, so it sits fourth. 5) risk_parity is a covariance-based risk-structured method with the smallest volatility breach among the risk-structured group (7.56% vs the 8% floor) and a drawdown of -20.3%. It fills the family-span requirement. Its reviewers note that the effective-N figure measures capital dispersion, not risk dispersion. My first choice beats my fifth because black_litterman is fully compliant with real drawdown margin and a return near the 7% range, whereas risk_parity breaches the volatility floor and would need a blending partner to be usable. I flag pc_researcher. It breaches return, volatility and tracking error, holds about 70% in short Treasuries and cash, and two reviewers found that its 0.60 Sharpe does not reconcile with its own claim that max Sharpe is about 0.48. The CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, since its orthogonality is a design feature.
